Package hadur2.core.move

Class ShotDodgePlanner

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.move.ShotDodgePlanner
public final class ShotDodgePlanner extends Object
DODGE-6: Hadur's own shot-dodge planner, inspired by Saguaro's ShotDodger (its ideas: score a path by its clearance from the predicted bullet, add the enemy's distance, learn from misses; no code or data of it): against a gun that fires one simple aim, plan a path on which that aim's bullets miss us, as far from them as the field allows. The paths are our surf's stop points, the experts our simple aims (DODGE-1), the band each bullet is given our own misses. Off by default; SurfMover hands it the tick only when the duel switches it on for the opponent and ShotDodger.planActive().

Why. DODGE-2's three-option surf knew Machete's bullet exactly (190 of 194 matched) and still took the same damage as without it (2,150 a battle, dodge-smoke run2..run5): orbit either way or stop cannot reach a safe spot at close range, and a 0/1 danger floored at 0.1 does not say how near a miss was. Saguaro instead searches many paths and scores each by the clearance its bullets leave.

  • Paths. Drive to a point and stop there: standing still, and the points reached at POINT_TICKS ticks along 12 straight headings and along both orbits of the first wave's source (wall-smoothed, the surf's attack angle toward the desired distance), each until every wave planned for has passed.
  • Waves. Up to 3 surfable waves whose expert bullet is known.
  • Score. For each wave, the precise intersection of the path's states with it: a path on which the expert's bullet falls inside it (within ShotDodger.MARGIN, at the share our bullet shadows let through) costs 1.0E9 times the bullet's damage, so it is taken only when every path is hit, and then the one hit least; otherwise the bullet's damage over the square of the clearance in radians (Saguaro's damage / (gfDistance * MEA)^2). Plus Saguaro's 2500 / d^2, d the least distance along the path to the enemy extrapolated at its last heading and speed.
  • Commitment. The path is kept until the waves planned for or the expert change, we are more than 2.0 px off it, or 5 ticks have passed (the enemy moves).

Angles are radians on Robocode's compass; distances in px; times in ticks.
